_meta.purpose: One entry per GitHub issue: what changed, where, how it was checked and what is left. Read this before starting an issue; update it in the same pull request that does the work.

status_values.in_progress: Someone is working on it; assignee and branch are set
status_values.on_hold: Do not start until the on-hold label is removed
status_values.in_review: Work is in an open pull request
status_values.ready_for_review: Implemented and verified on a feature branch; not merged

how_to_update: Starting an issue: set status to in_progress, fill assignee and branch, and assign yourself on GitHub
Finishing: set status to done, fill commit (hash, date, message, files), changes, verification and deviations_from_issue
Changing something a finished issue built: add an entry to that issue's revisions with the commit and a one-line summary
Work that belongs to no single issue goes in other_changes
Anything the next person must know goes in follow_ups
After a batch of work, add a dated record to the top of entries, including anything changed outside the repo and anything not verified

sections.entries: Dated records of a batch of work, newest first: what changed, the numbers that moved, changes made outside the repo, what was and was not verified
sections.issues: Current state of every GitHub issue
sections.other_changes: Work that belongs to no single issue

issues.title: Incident interpretation endpoint and validator

commit.message: A1: Incident interpretation endpoint, with an AI suggestion on the comparison

changes: server/: a small Node server with POST /incident/interpret and GET /health, run with npm run server. It listens on this machine only, and the dev server forwards /incident to it, so the browser never talks to the model
src/incident/interpretation.ts: the six-field answer format, the JSON schema given to the model (it lists the real segment ids), and the validator every model answer must pass
Provider: AI Squared's Bolt (bolt-instruct-v2) through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, called with Node's built-in fetch. The model returns its reading through one function call, record_incident
The model is sent the report text, each segment's id and name, and the answer format. Nothing else
A model answer that fails any check is discarded whole and returned as an error with the reasons; there is no partial incident
server/ai-tests.ts (npm run ai:tests): asks the real model the five test reports and writes docs/ai-tests.md; --check prints without writing
A new pipeline job, Live AI check on the five test reports, runs them on GitHub with the LLM_API_KEY repository secret and puts the table on the run's summary page
.env.example and the README record the provider, the variables, the endpoint's answers and the network note
verification: npm run build, typecheck, lint and test pass (244 tests with A1 alone, 49 new); npm run sanity passes (48 checks with A1 alone, 3 new)

Unit tests give the server canned model answers for all five test reports: each correct answer passes, and an invented segment, a quote that is not in the report, an extra field, a missing structured answer and broken JSON are each refused
The real server was started with node: with the AI off it answers 503 not_configured, and through a stand-in model on this machine a report is followed end to end
Tests confirm the key appears in the Authorization header only, and in no response, error or log line; the build check confirms no server-side name is in the browser bundle
deviations_from_issue: Acceptance criterion 1 is met with Claude, not with Bolt: docs/ai-tests.md records the real answers of Claude models to the five test reports, all as expected. Bolt, the provider the team named, is still unreachable from the venue network, so its answers are not recorded
The issue's Vite-only stack gained a dev proxy entry and two npm scripts; no dependency was added
Evidence is compared with line breaks and repeated spaces collapsed; otherwise it must match the report exactly

Beyond the issue's rules, the validator also rejects any field outside the six, a duration on a non-closure, a duration over 24 hours, and a closure with no segment that does not ask for clarification
One dependency was added after all: @anthropic-ai/sdk, for the Claude provider the owner asked for. The Bolt path still uses none
follow_ups: Record the real answers: run npm run ai:tests on a network that can reach the model, or read the Live AI check job's summary once the branch is pushed

Whether Bolt honours a forced function call is unverified. If the service refuses the request, the server asks once more without it; if the model answers in JSON text, that is accepted and checked the same way

The repository secret LLM_API_KEY and the variables LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL and LLM_PROVIDER were set on GitHub on 2026-11-14. Anyone with write access can read the secret through a workflow change; the key appears to be a shared event key
For the demo: on the venue network the AI call fails, so the manual-entry path in A2 (#16) will be what the dispatcher sees unless the laptop is on another network
The feature service now has more segments than src/data; when the importer is updated, the model's segment list follows automatically because it is read from segments.json

entries.title: Claude API as a second model provider, tested for real, with a model comparison
entries.summary: The server can now use the Claude API in place of Bolt, chosen by one setting. With a one-day key from the owner, four Claude models were asked the five test reports and three suggestions through the app's own server code. After three fixes to the instructions and one to a check, all four models passed everything in three consecutive runs. Claude Opus 5.5 is recommended and is the default.

commits.message: Add the Claude API as a second model provider, tested for real

numbers_that_moved: Dependencies: one added, @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.8.0, used by the server only
First real run: 4 of 5 reports read correctly per model, and between 1 and 3 of 3 suggestions passing; final three runs: 5 of 5 and 3 of 3 for every model
decisions: LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic selects Claude; any other value keeps the OpenAI-compatible path used for Bolt. Claude has its own variables (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_MODEL), so both sets can sit in .env and the Bolt key is never sent to Claude
Claude is called through Anthropic's official SDK, with the answer shape enforced by structured outputs; the server's validator still checks every answer
The SDK is always given the address api.anthropic.com and the server's own key, so it cannot pick up an address or credential from the surrounding environment; a test confirms this
If Claude declines a request for a policy reason, the API retries on its default fallback model; the model that actually answered is recorded
The default model is claude-opus-5-5 and stays so until a real run; ANTHROPIC_MODEL changes it
The prompts no longer say how to deliver the answer; each provider adds that itself (a function call for Bolt, a JSON object for Claude)
A segment id written in a report settles which segment is meant; a general area such as 'near the port' names no segment. Both were added to the instructions after the first real run
The AI's sentence may use names the figures already use (a shipment or segment id) and the word CO2; any actual figure is still refused. The target length, 200 characters, is now stated to the model
Tokens are counted for refused answers too, so the cost comparison is not skewed

Recommended model: Claude Opus 5.5. It was as accurate as the others, and on the one close trade-off (S-07) it made no suggestion, as the instructions ask; Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 suggested Reroute there
verification: npm run typecheck, lint and test pass (512 tests)
Real Claude API, through server/ai-tests.ts: three consecutive runs of 8 questions on each of 4 models, 96 answers, all passing; recorded in docs/ai-tests.md and docs/ai-model-comparison.md

Viewed in the browser with the real server and Claude Opus 5.5: S-01 showed Reroute with three confirmed reasons and three things it gives up; S-07 showed no suggestion with the AI's sentence; no option was pressed in either case
Structured outputs, the fallback setting and low effort were accepted by the API for all four models
not_verified: Bolt is still unreached, so A1's test record is from Claude, not from the provider the team named
Eight synthetic questions cannot rank the models finely, and no report written by a real dispatcher was tried
The fallback after a declined request never triggered, so that path is covered by unit tests only
Committed locally, not pushed
known_gaps: The pipeline's Live AI check still uses Bolt's secret and variables; running it on Claude needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repository secret
The Claude key in the local .env was created to expire after one day
outside_the_repo: A Claude API key supplied by the owner was written to the ignored .env in this working copy; about 20 small API calls' worth of spend per full comparison run, seven runs in all (well under two dollars by the script's estimate)

commits.message: A1: Incident interpretation endpoint, with an AI suggestion on the comparison

rule_change.rule: Tracker rule 4: No single "best option", ranking or ethics score anywhere
rule_change.decided_by: arturoidelgado1998, the repository owner, on 2026-11-14, after being told it conflicts with the rule
rule_change.what_changed: An AI suggestion can be requested per shipment. The comparison table still ranks and scores nothing, and the words best and recommended are still never shown
rule_change.not_done: The tracker issue (#1) text has not been edited, and the rest of the team has not been asked

decisions: The suggestion is shown only when asked for, to limit the pull of an answer the dispatcher did not seek
The model returns no figures. It names measures; the dashboard prints the values from its own data, and a number in the model's sentence makes the whole answer invalid
A reason is accepted only if the suggested option really is better on that measure; what the suggestion gives up is computed from the figures and never shortened
A slot request can be suggested only when no other option is on track, and is always shown as pending
The browser checks the server's answer again against the facts it sent, so the panel shows nothing it cannot verify itself

What the AI is asked to weigh is one constant, WEIGHING, shown to the dispatcher word for word: the appointment first, then schools and disadvantaged communities passed, then duty time, cost, miles and emissions, and no suggestion when it is close
The suggestion's state lives in the panel, not in the reducer, so it cannot reach the decisions or the totals

entries.title: Added sanity checks and a pipeline job that runs them
entries.summary: A new suite checks that the project as a whole still works: the repository, this change log, the production build, and the built app driven through its main flow in a real browser. The pipeline runs it on every pull request and push to main and staging.

commits.message: Add sanity checks and run them in the pipeline

checks: Repository (9 checks): npm scripts named in the README and workflows, README layout, valid Python in scripts/, no tracked .env, keys or build output, .env.example has names only, browser code reads only VITE_ variables

Change log (9 checks): sections, dates newest first, unique issue numbers and codes, known statuses, summary counts match, worked-on issues have an assignee, branch, commit, changes and verification, references resolve, listed files still exist

Build (4 checks): page has its root and title, every script and stylesheet it loads exists, the ArcGIS map is one separate chunk and first-load JavaScript is under 500 kB, no server-side variable names in the bundle

Browser (6 checks): starts with no errors and one card per shipment, the closure moves the affected shipments to Needs review, the reference shipment shows Wait, Reroute and Request later slot, every shipment opens in both scenarios, Reset clears everything, the real map chunk loads and the view starts cleanly where it can
pipeline: Job 'Sanity checks on the built app' added to .github/workflows/advisory-checks.yml: npm ci, install headless Chromium, npm run build, npm run test:sanity
The workflow itself was added in 9511f83 and had no change log record until now
project: package.json: scripts test:sanity and sanity; dev dependency playwright 1.65.0
vitest.sanity.config.ts keeps the sanity checks out of npm test; tsconfig.sanity.json and eslint.config.js cover sanity/
README: a Sanity checks section and the sanity/ folder in the layout
change_log: summary.pull_requests: #26 marked merged into staging (4296815); #27 (staging to main) added
G2 (#20) follow_ups: the map fallback gap described under known_gaps

decisions: The browser values are read from src/data, so refreshing the data from the feature service does not break the checks

The dashboard checks hold the map chunk back: without WebGL the SDK throws an uncaught error, which would fail them on a runner with no graphics. This also exercises the pane's fallback in a real browser
One check loads the real map. Where the browser has WebGL and reaches Esri, the view must start with no uncaught errors; otherwise the check passes with a warning that the view was not checked
scripts/import_map_data.py --check is not in the pipeline: it depends on the live feature service, which anyone can edit, so it would fail unrelated pull requests
verification: npm run sanity: 28 of 28 checks pass locally (macOS, Node 24, headless Chromium), in about 8 seconds after the build
npm run lint, typecheck and test pass (84 unit tests, unchanged)
The real map view started in headless Chromium with no uncaught errors

Checks fail when they should, each tried and then undone: a wrong count in this file, a listed file renamed, a server-side variable read in src, a missing npm script named in the README, the map imported without lazy loading, a crash on one shipment
With WebGL turned off in the browser, all six browser checks still pass and the map check prints its warning
not_verified: The new job has not run on GitHub: the commit is local and has not been pushed
Whether the map view starts on GitHub's Linux runner. The browser is started with software WebGL allowed, but this was only tried on macOS
Docker was not running, so the checks were not tried in a Linux container
known_gaps: Map fallback: with no WebGL, or with Esri's servers unreachable, the map view never starts and the pane does not show 'The map could not load'; that message only appears when the map chunk fails to load. Without WebGL the SDK also throws an uncaught error. Not fixed here; noted on G2 (#20)
The change log check on listed files will fail a pull request that removes or renames a file without listing the old path under deleted
The key scan looks for a few common key formats; it is not a full secret scanner
Issues #19 and #20 stay in_review until staging reaches main

data: scripts/import_map_data.py reads the feature service, rebuilds src/data and pre-calculates the sample responses; --check verifies without writing
